validity.researcher_notes: MAJOR FINDING -- this is not a cancelled project, it was built. Kinder Morgan's Texas Intrastate Pipelines group signed a 20-year firm transportation agreement with SK E&S LNG, LLC in December 2014 to invest >$150M and build ~40 miles of pipe from its Tejas mainline to an interconnect with Freeport LNG's existing pipeline at Stratton Ridge, TX, to support Freeport LNG Train III (LNG World News, 2014-12-09, Wayback capture -- name_found on 'SK LNG'). Kinder Morgan's own SEC 8-K exhibit filed 2015-01-21 restates the identical $150M/320,000 Dth/d/Quintana Island/Train III facts (name_found on 'SK E&S'). This is exactly the project the sheet calls 'SK Pipeline' -- SK is the counterparty's name. I then traced KMI's disclosures forward year by year and found CONTINUOUS, UNBROKEN progress with no mention of suspension or cancellation at any point: the Q2/Q3 2016 8-Ks describe it as 'Phase 2' of a combined 'Texas Intrastate Crossover' project (est. cost $161M then $326M total both phases) 'supported by a long-term commitment from SK E&S LNG, LLC ... to service the Freeport LNG export facility,' expected in service late 2018; the FY2016 10-K (filed 2017-02-10) still shows it active, now targeting 3Q2019, same SK E&S language; the FY2017 10-K (filed 2018-02-09) unchanged; the FY2018 10-K (filed 2019-02-08) shows Phase 2 slipped to 2Q2020 at $298M; and the FY2019 10-K (filed 2020-02-12) states plainly 'Phase 1 and Phase 2 are in service' at a final $288M. A contemporaneous, independent trade-press snapshot mid-stream -- Pipeline & Gas Journal's 'Ongoing Projects' list, October 2018 issue (PN1018-Ongoing-Projects.pdf, verified name_found='SK Pipeline' literally) -- lists 'SK Pipeline' by that exact name under Kinder Morgan Inc., 30-inch diameter, West Columbia TX-Stratton Ridge TX, 320 MDth/d, completion 3Q2019, 'to support Train III export capacity as part of the Freeport LNG Export Project' -- pinning the PGJ project-list entry to the identical SK E&S commitment tracked in KMI's own filings. GEM's ShelvedYear=2016 and CancelledYear=2018 (ShelvedCancelledType=inferred, i.e. GUESSED from apparent dormancy after the initial 2014 press coverage went quiet) are contradicted by every one of these filings -- the project was never dormant, it was mid-construction the whole time, and it was completed. Recommend Status->operating and clearing the Shelved/Cancelled fields entirely (see status_reviews for the full proposed edit and Shelved/Cancelled [ref] fills below for why those units are UNRESOLVED rather than re-sourced). CAVEAT on precision: none of my sources independently confirm that the FINAL as-built pipe segment retained the exact original 40-mile/30-inch West Columbia-Stratton Ridge alignment once it was folded into the larger, multi-shipper 'Texas Intrastate Crossover Expansion' (which also serves Cheniere Corpus Christi LNG and CFE/Mexico from the Katy Hub) -- KMI's disclosures track the SK E&S COMMERCIAL COMMITMENT continuously to completion, not a discrete as-built map of this specific lateral. I searched SEC full-text search for 'Kinder Morgan' + 'Stratton Ridge' for a second, non-KMI confirmation of completion and found only unrelated pre-2011 filings about KMI's separate Stratton Ridge gas STORAGE facility; WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted) so I could not chase a Freeport LNG-side or FERC/RRC confirmation of the exact built route. The status-change evidence itself is therefore single-origin (Kinder Morgan's own SEC filings, tier=medium per the independence rule) even though it is unusually strong (five consecutive annual/quarterly SEC filings over 2014-2020, unbroken).

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is the single most important finding on this row (flagged explicitly by the batch brief as a project to test): GEM's 'cancelled' (ShelvedYear=2016, CancelledYear=2018, ShelvedCancelledType=inferred -- i.e. GUESSED from apparent silence, never a sourced cancellation event) is wrong. I traced Kinder Morgan's own SEC disclosures for this exact SK E&S/Freeport LNG Train III commitment across FIVE consecutive filings spanning 2014-2020 (the original Dec-2014 8-K announcing it; the mid-2016 8-Ks describing it as 'Phase 2' of a combined 'Texas Intrastate Crossover' project, still active; the FY2016 and FY2017 10-Ks, both still active and targeting 3Q2019; the FY2018 10-K showing the target slipped to 2Q2020 at $298M; and the FY2019 10-K stating flatly 'Phase 1 and Phase 2 are in service' at a final $288M) -- there is no gap, no suspension notice, no withdrawal, at any point. A contemporaneous, independently-published trade-press project list (Pipeline & Gas Journal's 'Ongoing Projects,' October 2018) corroborates mid-stream: it lists 'SK Pipeline' under Kinder Morgan as an ACTIVE project with a 3Q2019 completion target, not as cancelled or shelved. My working theory for how GEM's row went wrong: whoever built it likely found only the original Dec-2014 announcement (the two citations harvested from the gem.wiki page are exactly those two: the LNG World News piece and, oddly, an October-2018 PGJ Ongoing Projects citation that -- read carefully -- actually shows the project STILL ACTIVE, not cancelled) and, seeing no later news specifically using the name 'SK Pipeline' after the project was folded into KMI's larger 'Texas Intrastate Crossover Expansion' branding in 2016, inferred a 2016 shelving and a 2018 cancellation from the apparent silence -- exactly the trap the dormancy-inference rule exists to avoid, except here the underlying project was never actually silent, it just changed the name analysts describe it under. Recommend Status->operating, clear ShelvedYear/CancelledYear/ShelvedCancelledType entirely (a built project cannot be shelved-then-cancelled), and keep StartYear1=2019 as the best-supported year while flagging (see the Start [ref] fill) that the actual in-service date could be as late as early 2020. Independence caveat: every source in this chain but the PGJ list traces to Kinder Morgan itself (SEC filings are legally binding disclosures, not press-release fluff, but still one corporate origin) -- I searched SEC full-text search for a non-KMI party mentioning 'Stratton Ridge' post-2014 and found nothing relevant (only unrelated pre-2011 filings about KMI's separate gas-storage facility of the same name), and WebSearch was unavailable this session (session budget exhausted at 200/200 calls, evidently from the other 44 parallel subagents in this batch) so I could not chase an independent Freeport LNG-side or Texas RRC/PHMSA confirmation of completion. Tier reflects that single-origin caveat despite the unusual strength (5 consecutive years of unbroken SEC disclosure) of the evidence.
